conventions: Python is uv-managed; use `uv run python ...`, `uvx <tool>`, `uv tool install <tool>`.
Node.js uses the latest LTS (26.x) from the official tarball; npm prefix is ~/.local, registry is registry.npmmirror.com.
Two JDKs: JAVA_HOME from apt openjdk-17-jdk for Android 4.4 builds; JDK25_HOME=~/code-tools/jdk-25 (java25 wrapper) for Ghidra/REA.
Android SDK includes API 19 (Android 4.4) and API 37 (Android 17), build-tools 19.1/35/37, NDK 29/30.
Android SDK lives in ~/code-tools/android-sdk; adb is under platform-tools.
REA MCP is launched by ~/.local/bin/rea-mcp via `npx -y rea-agents@latest mcp`; never run `rea-agents setup --client`.
All installs are user-space; no sudo required after `apt update/upgrade`.
Proxy 192.168.31.50:7890 is used on-demand only by setup.sh download helpers (or explicit `proxy` wrapper); never exported from ~/.bashrc. LAN and direct downloads bypass it.

config_facts.title: Python is uv-managed
config_facts.value: uv run python script.py | uvx <tool> | uv tool install <tool>
config_facts.usage: Prefer uv-managed CPython 3.12. A system python3 exists from apt, but project work should use `uv run` so dependencies come from uv.lock.

config_facts.title: npm registry mirror
config_facts.usage: npm install / npx use the npmmirror registry; no proxy is configured in npm itself.

config_facts.title: pnpm registry mirror
config_facts.usage: pnpm uses the same npmmirror registry as npm.

config_facts.title: GitHub release/raw accelerator
config_facts.usage: For GitHub release assets and raw.githubusercontent.com URLs, prefix the FULL original https:// URL with the accelerator host: https://github.allproxy.dpdns.org/https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/releases/... Host-only replacement returns 404/502.
config_facts.notes: Verified 2026-11-25 for Ghidra release download. Keep normal github.com for GitHub API and git clone unless the user says otherwise.

config_facts.title: On-demand HTTP(S) proxy
config_facts.usage: Use only for specific blocked downloads via download helpers in setup.sh / rea-setup.sh. Never export globally from ~/.bashrc; LAN and direct traffic must bypass it.
config_facts.notes: GitHub API and small files use the proxy; PyPI and Android SDK downloads are direct (proxy causes TLS errors / bad_record_mac).

config_facts.title: GitHub CLI
config_facts.usage: Use gh for GitHub auth/API operations. `gh auth login` has been completed; it is also the git credential helper for github.com.
config_facts.notes: gh 2.105.0. For non-Git tools that need the proxy, set it per command; gh does not read git http.proxy for API calls.

config_facts.title: Install preference
config_facts.value: apt (sudo, user-run) -> official tarball / GitHub release via accelerator -> user-space tools
config_facts.usage: Prefer apt for system packages (run by user), then official release archives downloaded through the accelerator, then uv/npm user-space installs.
config_facts.notes: No sudo is available to the agent; apt commands are handed to the user.

config_facts.title: REA MCP single source of truth
config_facts.usage: Clients point to this absolute wrapper path with no environment/env block. REA is disabled by default; connect only when needed. Never run `rea-agents setup --client`; skill-only updates are safe.
config_facts.notes: Launch: ~/code-tools/nodejs/bin/npx -y rea-agents@latest mcp. Only free tools are configured; IDA/JEB/Hopper are paid and skipped; Kuna is Windows-only per REA docs.
